title: Sealed Classes
objectives: Restrict which types can extend a class/interface
Combine sealed types with pattern matching for exhaustiveness

sections.markdown: A sealed class/interface (Java 17+) explicitly lists which classes may extend or implement it, giving you a closed, known set of subtypes.
Sealed types + records + pattern matching give Java **algebraic data types**: a fixed set of shapes the compiler can check exhaustively, eliminating the 'forgot a case' bug.
Use sealed hierarchies when the set of subtypes is meant to be closed (results, states, AST nodes). It documents intent and unlocks exhaustive switches.

flashcards.back: The compiler can check the switch is exhaustive — no default needed, no missed case.
